tools.reports: The load test's reports, newest first: per run its id, scenario, start, how it ended (completed, stopped, aborted by a rule, closed with rBrowser), requests, requests per second, failure rate and p95 in ms. Read only: MCP can neither start, change nor stop a load test.
tools.report: One load test report (the newest without id): scenario, profile, targets with their standing, how it ended and which abort rule stopped it, totals (requests, failures, rate, p50/p95/p99, min, max, mean in ms), failures by kind, statuses, each step's share and the series of seconds. Read only.
tools.compare: Two load test reports a and b side by side - requests, requests per second, failure rate, p50, p95, p99 - and what changed from a to b. Read only.
tools.panel: The load test panel's own calls; not an MCP tool.

maxUsers.label: Most virtual users
maxUsers.description: The most virtual users a load test may run (50 by default). A scenario with more is refused until you raise this. Not writable over MCP.
maxUsers.help: rBrowser has no ceiling of its own: this setting is the one limit of the users of a run. Raise it only for a server you own or may test, and that can take it.

maxRps.label: Most requests per second
maxRps.description: The most requests per second of a load test, all users together (200 by default); a scenario without a rate of its own is held to it. Not writable over MCP.
maxRps.help: Every run is paced to its scenario's rate or to this one, whichever is lower; a scenario that asks for more is refused until you raise this.

maxDurationS.label: Longest run (seconds)
maxDurationS.description: The longest a load test may run, ramps included (300 seconds, 5 minutes, by default). Not writable over MCP.
maxDurationS.help: A scenario whose ramp up, hold and ramp down add up to more is refused until you raise this. Stop ends a run at any time.

allowedHosts.label: Confirmed hosts
allowedHosts.description: Hosts outside this project's own sites you confirmed are yours or yours to test; kept on this machine only. Remove one to be asked again. Not writable over MCP.
allowedHosts.help: Without asking, a load test sends only to the project's own sites (start URL and environments) and to this machine. Any other host needs your confirmation in the load test panel that it is yours or that you may test it; it is kept in config.local.json, without scheme or port.
